title: Snakes and ladders: a small game engine

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own snakes-and-ladders design case and kata, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

scenario: The hostel's gaming club wants a snakes-and-ladders engine for its app. Dice rolls come from the app; the engine owns the board and the rules. Design the classes and write the engine so the club can later add house rules without rewriting it.

clarifying_questions.a: Configurable size; snakes go down, ladders go up; a square has at most one jump.

clarifying_questions.q: What if a roll overshoots the last square?
clarifying_questions.a: The player stays where they are (exact finish).

clarifying_questions.q: Can a jump chain into another jump?

clarifying_questions.a: The game is over; further rolls are refused.

functional: Configure a board with snakes and ladders, validating them
Take turns among 1 or more players with given dice rolls
Apply jumps, the exact-finish rule and the win

non_functional.name: Extensibility
non_functional.target: house rules (extra turns, bounce-back) change one method

non_functional.name: Determinism
non_functional.target: the same rolls always give the same game

entities.name: Board
entities.responsibility: Size and the jump table; answers where a player lands from a square.

entities.name: Game
entities.responsibility: Players, positions, whose turn it is, the move rules and the winner.

entities.name: Driver (Main)
entities.responsibility: Reads commands, validates jumps, prints results.

patterns.name: Separate board data from game rules
patterns.why: The board only maps squares; rules about turns and winning live in Game, so a different board never touches rules.

patterns.name: Turn policy in one method
patterns.why: Who plays next is decided in one place, so house rules like 'a six gives another turn' change only that method.

diagram.alt: Class diagram: Game has a Board, a list of players, a map of positions, the current turn and a winner; Board has a size and a map of jumps.

data.source:
classDiagram
  class Board {
    size
    jumps: Map~int,int~
    land(square) int
  }
  class Game {
    players: List
    pos: Map~player,int~
    turn
    winner
    move(roll)
    nextTurn(roll)
  }
  Game o-- Board

kata.io_protocol:
| Command | Prints | |---|---| | `BOARD ` | `board of ` | | `SNAKE ` / `LADDER ` | `snake a -> b` / `ladder a -> b`, or `error: bad snake a b` | | `PLAYERS ...` | `players: ...` | | `ROLL <1-6>` | `

rolls , -> ` (with ` (ladder)` or ` (snake)`), or `

rolls , stays at `; on reaching the last square a second line `

wins`; after that `game over:

won` | A snake needs 0 < tail < head < size; a ladder 0 < foot < top ≤ size. Anything else: `error: bad command `.

rubric.criterion: Kata tests pass, including the house rule.
Board holds only squares and jumps; Game holds turns, positions and rules.
Exact finish, single jump per move and game-over are each handled once, clearly.
The extra-turn rule touches only the turn policy.
Readable names and small methods (AI feedback, advice only).

concept_checks.stem: Board of 20, a player on 17 rolls 5. What happens?
concept_checks.explanation: 17 + 5 overshoots 20, so the exact-finish rule keeps the player in place.

concept_checks.stem: Where should 'a six gives another turn' be implemented?
options: In the method that decides the next turn
concept_checks.explanation: Turn policy lives in one method.

concept_checks.stem: Why keep jumps in a map from square to destination?
options: Landing becomes one O(1) lookup, and snakes and ladders are the same idea
concept_checks.explanation: A jump is just 'from here, go there'.

concept_checks.stem: Why validate that a snake's head is above its tail when configuring?
options: So an invalid board is refused at setup instead of producing strange games later

follow_ups: Add a 'bounce back' rule: overshooting moves you back from the last square by the excess.
Support saving and loading a game in progress.
Make the dice pluggable so tests can use fixed rolls and the app random ones.

revision_card.front: Snakes and ladders LLD: classes, the one-lookup trick, and where house rules go?
revision_card.back: Board (size, jumps map) and Game (players, positions, turn, winner). Landing = jumps.get(square, square). Exact finish: overshoot means stay. House rules (extra turn on 6) live in the single nextTurn method.
